deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page, so there is nothing to reconstruct. Folio 57v is page 2 of a printed lecture catalogue: the 'Verzeichniß der Vorlesungen' of the Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität zu Berlin for the summer semester of 12 April to 14 August 1847. The preceding page carries the title and the theology section. This page is entirely the law section ('Rechtsgelahrtheit'). It lists, with days and hours, courses given by:
- Schmidt (method of legal study; Roman legal history after Puchta; Pandects; Pandekten-Practicum)
- Röstell (encyclopaedia and methodology; church law; Protestant church constitution)
- Collmann (encyclopaedia; German state and legal history; German state and federal law)
- Heydemann (natural law / legal philosophy)
- Stahl (legal philosophy, church law, marriage law)
- Rudorff (Roman law in the Middle Ages; Roman legal history to Justinian; Pandects; inheritance law)
- Keller (Institutes; bills of exchange law; an exegetical collegium)
- Gneist (Institutes and antiquities; criminal law; criminal procedure)
- Dirksen (Pandects after Mühlenbruch; inheritance law)
- v. Lancizolle (sources of German state and legal history)
- Homeyer (German private law after Kraut; peasant law)
- Häberlin (feudal law)
- Heffter (European and German state law)
- v. Richthofen (German state and federal law; German estates)
- Richter (Protestant church constitution; examinatorium in church law)
- Berner (criminal law and procedure)
- v. Daniels (German criminal law compared with French; criminal procedure; philosophical theories of punishment)

The document fits Riemann's biography. He moved from Göttingen to Berlin for the summer semester of 1847 and studied there until 1849, attending Jacobi, Dirichlet, Steiner and Eisenstein. He presumably kept the whole catalogue, most likely for its mathematics and natural-science listings, which would appear on later pages. This law page survives only because it is part of the same printed sheet. There are no marginal annotations, underlinings or handwritten marks visible on the page.

results.what: Printed Berlin University lecture catalogue, summer semester 1847, law faculty section (non-mathematical document preserved in Riemann's Nachlass)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics and no handwriting by Riemann. It is a printed Berlin course catalogue for summer 1847. That semester matches Riemann's well-documented move to Berlin, so its presence in his papers is entirely expected.
transcription_corrections: 'Criminalprocefs' (twice) should be 'Criminalproceſs' (long s), i.e. Criminalprozess; the machine transcription renders the long s as 'f' here, inconsistently with 'Grundriſs', 'Einschluſs' and 'Preuſsischen' elsewhere.
'11-1Uhr' and '10-11Uhr' lack a space in the transcription ('11-1 Uhr'); this is cosmetic, and the print itself is tight here.
The line 'des Römischen Rechts, Hr. Prof. Gneist fünf-' is partly obscured in the image (top half of the letters lost). The transcription's reading is the plausible reconstruction.
The name read as 'Heffter' appears in the print as 'Heffter', with the second f possibly damaged; the transcription is correct.
